title: A model structure is determined by its cofibrations and its fibrant objects
statement: Use the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a category carrying two model structures $(C_1,F_1,W_1)$ and $(C_2,F_2,W_2)$, with cofibrations $C_i$, fibrations $F_i$ and weak equivalences $W_i$. Suppose that $C_1=C_2$ and that an object of $\mathcal M$ is fibrant for the first structure if and only if it is fibrant for the second. Then $W_1=W_2$ and $F_1=F_2$. In particular the two structures have the same trivial cofibrations and the same trivial fibrations, and an adjunction is a Quillen adjunction, respectively a Quillen equivalence, for one of them exactly when it is for the other.

source.place: A. Joyal, The theory of quasi-categories and its applications (CRM Barcelona, 2008), Appendix E, Proposition E.2.14 (a model structure is determined by its class of cofibrations and its class of fibrant objects). Not archived in literature/; WANTED. No Stacks tag.
